dedupe_keys.name: unchain case study 3 economic effects of adapting critical infrastructure in the mannheim metropolitan area

description: This case study from the UNCHAIN project applied Impact Chain based climate risk and vulnerability assessment to critical infrastructure in the Mannheim metropolitan area in Germany. It started from relevant parts of the German national Impact Chains, built regional Impact Chains from them and then traced risk factors down to the units, processes and activities of companies along their value chain; on economic effects it assessed more frequent periods of low water on the Rhine and their effect on inland waterway transport of goods needed for energy production. The lessons-learned report (deliverable D3.4.3, 31 March 2022) was written by Erich Rome, Daniel Lückerath and Katharina Milde of Fraunhofer IAIS. A short German version and a long English version are available free on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: it is a qualitative participatory method report, not a quantitative loss model, and results are specific to the stakeholders involved. It shows how cross-sector dependencies between waterways, energy supply and industry can be mapped for adaptation planning; a related record is the MYRIAD-EU multi-risk toolkit.
